# Coding Conventions {#sec-app-conventions .unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note title="Status: complete first draft"}
:::

A condensed reference of NebulaStream's C++ conventions, intended
to make code listings throughout the book self-explanatory. The
authoritative source is
`/Users/zeuchste/git/nebulastream/docs/coding_guidelines.md` (~346
lines) and `docs/naming_conventions.md` (~60 lines); this
appendix summarises.

---

## B.1 Formatting {#sec-app-formatting}

- **clang-format-19**, WebKit-based style.
- **140-column line limit.** Generous compared to the typical 80
  or 100; the team prefers to break long expressions only when
  unavoidable.
- **4-space indent.** Spaces, not tabs.
- **`#pragma once`** for header guards; no include guards.
- **Angle brackets** (`#include <foo/Bar.hpp>`) for all includes;
  never relative paths (`#include "../bar.hpp"`).
- **No `using namespace` in global scope of headers.** Avoids
  cross-translation-unit name pollution.

The `format` and `check-format` CMake targets enforce this.

---

## B.2 Naming {#sec-app-naming}

- **Classes/structs:** `CamelCase` (e.g., `QueryOptimizer`,
  `TupleBuffer`, `WindowedAggregationLogicalOperator`).
- **Methods, functions, variables, parameters:** `camelBack`
  (e.g., `optimize()`, `logicalPlan`, `queryId`).
- **Enum classes:** the enum and its entries are both `CamelCase`
  (e.g., `enum class Color : int8_t { Red, Green };`).
- **Constants:** `UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `INVALID_QUERY_ID`,
  `DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE`).
- **Type specialisations:** `{Spec}{Interface}` pattern. A `Source`
  implementation for files is `FileSource`; a `Sink` implementation
  for printing is `PrintSink`. The pattern makes plugin types
  greppable.

---

## B.3 Error handling {#sec-app-errors}

- **Bugs**: `INVARIANT` and `PRECONDITION` macros (Chapter 17).
  Compiled out in `Release` and `Benchmark` builds via
  `#define NO_ASSERT`.
- **Recoverable errors**: throw exceptions (by value), catch by
  `const&`. Typed exceptions only.
- **Expected-but-unsuccessful outcomes**: `std::expected<T,
  Exception>` or `std::optional<T>`.
- All exception types live in a single file:
  `nes-common/include/ExceptionDefinitions.inc`. Do not define
  exceptions elsewhere.

---

## B.4 Ownership {#sec-app-ownership}

- **Prefer value semantics** by default. Pass-by-value, return-by-
  value, prefer composition over containment-by-pointer.
- **`unique_ptr`** for exclusive ownership. The default for
  performance-critical code that needs heap allocation.
- **`shared_ptr`** only where ownership is genuinely shared. The
  atomic refcount is not free; use sparingly.
- **No raw `new` or `malloc`.** No raw pointers for ownership.
  Raw pointers are non-owning observers.
- **`static_cast` / `dynamic_cast`**, never C-style casts.

---

## B.5 Const-correctness and const by default {#sec-app-const}

- **`const` by default** — Rust-like. Mark variables `const`
  unless they need to mutate. Mark methods `const` unless they
  modify state.
- **Pass `const&` for non-trivial types** that the function does
  not need to mutate.
- **Return `const&` only when you can guarantee the lifetime** of
  the referenced object. Otherwise return by value.

---

## B.6 Other {#sec-app-other}

- **Operator overloads** (`+`, `-`, `<<`) preferred over named
  methods (`add()`, `toString()`) where natural. The `<<` operator
  for stream output is the canonical "to-string" mechanism.
- **`NAMEOF_TYPE(T)`** instead of `typeid(T).name()`. Avoids
  RTTI dependencies.
- **Structs for POD; classes for anything with non-public
  members.** A type with private state is a `class`; a type that
  is just data is a `struct`.

---

## B.7 Common abbreviations {#sec-app-abbrev}

In code and comments:

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `TB` | TupleBuffer |
| `BM` | BufferManager |
| `OP` | Operator |
| `LHS / RHS` | LeftHandSide / RightHandSide |
| `SS` | StringStream |

The full glossary is in Appendix C.
